chief_complaint: Shortness of breath and fatigue for the past week, worse with exertion.
diagnosis: Congestive Heart Failure (New York Heart Association Class II)
doctor_notes: Patient presents with symptoms suggestive of decompensated heart failure. Physical exam reveals mild pedal edema and bibasilar crackles.  Current medications for hypertension are noted.  BNP is elevated, supporting the diagnosis of CHF.  Started on diuretics and adjusted antihypertensive regimen.  Advised on fluid restriction and low-sodium diet.  Will monitor weight daily.  Patient is aware of warning signs of worsening symptoms.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: Good morning, Mrs. Vance. What brings you in today?

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: I've been feeling so tired lately, and it's getting harder to breathe, even just walking to the kitchen.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: How long has this been going on?

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: About a week now. It seems to be getting worse.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: I see. Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles?

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Yes, a little bit, especially at the end of the day.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: Okay, we'll need to run some tests to get a clearer picture. Based on your symptoms, we're going to investigate for heart failure.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: It's something we can manage, but it requires careful attention. We'll start by adjusting your medications and making some dietary recommendations. We'll also schedule you for a follow-up appointment soon.

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Thank you, doctor. I'll do whatever it takes.
